# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and recent userspace
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Do not prompt for any input during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, Git, CMake, and MPI libraries.
# Also install ca-certificates and dpkg-dev for multi-arch support and clean up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    dpkg-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes.
# They allow running as root, oversubscribing resources (common in CI/testing),
# and explicitly selecting the TCP network interface.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 \
    OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0 \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Set the final working directory for the application data
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command performs all build steps to optimize for a smaller image size.
# It creates a temporary build directory, clones and builds MFEM (a dependency),
# clones and builds the Laghos application, copies the resulting binary and data files
# to their final locations, and finally removes the temporary build directory.
RUN mkdir /build && cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Build and install the MFEM dependency ---
    # Clone the latest branch of the MFEM library
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git mfem && \
    # Create a separate directory for an out-of-source build, as required by MFEM.
    mkdir mfem/build && \
    cd mfem/build && \
    # Configure MFEM from the build directory, pointing to the source in the parent dir.
    # FIX: Correct the CMake variable to HYPRE_LIBRARIES (plural) to match build system.
    cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
            -DMFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
            -DMFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
            -DMFEM_USE_LAPACK=YES \
            -DMFEM_USE_HYPRE=ON \
            -DHYPRE_INCLUDE_DIRS=/usr/include/hypre \
            -DHYPRE_LIBRARIES=/usr/lib/$(dpkg-architecture -q DEB_HOST_MULTIARCH)/libHYPRE.so \
            -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=YES && \
    # Build and install MFEM to a system location (/usr/local)
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # Return to the main build directory to proceed with Laghos
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Build the Laghos application ---
    # Clone the latest branch of the Laghos application
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git Laghos && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos, pointing it to the location of the installed MFEM library
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # --- Stage final artifacts ---
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a directory on the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the final WORKDIR (/app)
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove the temporary build directory and all its contents
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the 'laghos' HPC application
# within a single pod on a Kubernetes cluster, suitable for an AWS CPU instance environment.
# It leverages the Flux Operator to manage the distributed execution of the application.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance running the laghos experiment.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploys the MiniCluster to the 'default' Kubernetes namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of tasks (e.g., MPI ranks) for the Flux job.
  # This will run 4 laghos processes within the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines the container that will run the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator automatically wraps this
      # with 'flux run -n <tasks> ...'. We assume 'laghos' is in the PATH and the
      # mesh file is in the default working directory.
      command: laghos -m cube_311_hex.mesh
      # This container runs the workload, not the launcher logic.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict, machine-readable log formatting.
    strict: true

  # Job Lifecycle Policies
  # Retain pods and resources after the job completes for debugging and inspection.
  cleanup: false

updates.reason: Previous run used only 4 tasks. This attempt targets a high-core-count, HPC-optimized instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scales the MPI tasks to match the 64 available vCPUs, which should dramatically increase parallelism and performance.

Performance degraded when scaling from 4 to 64 tasks, suggesting poor strong scaling. This attempt targets a modern 48-core AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) to test an intermediate level of parallelism, aiming for a better balance between computation and communication overhead.

Performance has consistently decreased with higher task counts (4->48->64), indicating poor strong scaling for this problem size. This attempt reduces parallelism to 24 tasks and switches to a modern Intel instance (c6in.12xlarge) to test an intermediate core count and a different CPU architecture.

The previous run at 24 tasks yielded the best performance (18.83). This attempt modestly increases parallelism to 32 tasks on a compute-optimized AMD instance (c6a.16xlarge) to explore if the peak performance is slightly higher before hitting the negative scaling observed at 48+ tasks.

The performance peaked at 18.84 with 24 tasks on a c6in.12xlarge instance. Subsequent attempts with both higher (32) and lower (4, initial run) task counts on various architectures resulted in lower performance. This suggests the optimal configuration for this problem size and instance selection has been found.

  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: laghos -m cube_311_hex.mesh
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
    launcher: false
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c6a.16xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 32

manager.name: Build and Deploy Laghos
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details: Ensure all globbed files from ./data from the root of the laghos codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch.

context.optimize:
Run cube_311_hex.mesh with laghos in the pwd. You MUST maximize the Major kernels total rate (megadofs x time steps / second). The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster,
so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types,
and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your
choice. You are still limited to one node.
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
  hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6in.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  r7iz.8xlarge, 16 vCPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6g.12xlarge, 48 vCPU, 192 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  t3a.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, AMD
  t3.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  t4g.2xlarge, 8 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  m6i.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6a.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, AMD
  m7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6i.16xlarge, 32 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6a.16xlarge, 32 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, AMD
  c7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  r6i.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  r6a.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 384 GiB Memory, AMD
  r7g.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 384 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  i4i.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  d3.4xlarge, 8 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, Intel
If you choose an ARM (Graviton) instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9. Otherwise, do not change or set it.
context.testing: Run cube_311_hex.mesh with laghos in the pwd
context.details:
You MUST run on only one node. 
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
